openai._comment: Authentication is an ordinary custom header rather than a dedicated credential field. OPENAI_API_KEY must hold the full header value including the 'Bearer ' scheme prefix - there is no separate scheme field to compose it for you.

anthropic._comment: Anthropic's REST API (including GET /v1/models used by model discovery) rejects any request without an anthropic-version header. It's configured here as a generic custom header rather than special-cased in code. Auth is the raw key with no scheme prefix, so ANTHROPIC_API_KEY holds it unmodified.

alibaba._comment: QWEN_API_KEY must hold the full header value including the 'Bearer ' scheme prefix - see the openai entry's comment.

zhipu._comment: GLM_API_KEY must hold the full header value including the 'Bearer ' scheme prefix - see the openai entry's comment.

moonshot._comment: KIMI_API_KEY must hold the full header value including the 'Bearer ' scheme prefix - see the openai entry's comment.

minimax._comment: MINIMAX_API_KEY must hold the full header value including the 'Bearer ' scheme prefix - see the openai entry's comment.

ollama._comment: Local, unauthenticated - no auth header configured, so ProxyMiddleware never injects one. See docs/router/unified-api-translation.md §4.1: Ollama's own /v1/chat/completions endpoint is already OpenAI-shaped end-to-end (request/response/streaming), so no payload translation is needed - ProxyMiddleware's existing pass-through forwarding handles it unchanged, same as the openai provider above. IsFree marks a local runtime that genuinely costs nothing, so its models report a known cost of 0 rather than an unknown one. This seeds a fresh install only: once model-routing.json exists, that file owns provider config - see docs/router/telemetry.md#pricing.

lmstudio._comment: Local, unauthenticated, same OpenAI-shaped end-to-end passthrough as ollama above - no IPayloadTranslator needed. EnableToolCallGuard is set here because small/quantized local models served by LM Studio have been observed echoing their own tool-call instructions back as literal text (e.g. '<tool_call>{...}</tool_call>' or a corrupted '<tools>...</tools>' variant) instead of a real OpenAI tool_calls delta/field - see docs/router/unified-api-translation.md §4.5. The flag is not specific to this provider name: it can be set on ollama above, or any other provider with no registered translator, if the same symptom shows up there too.

gemini._comment: Google AI Studio (generativelanguage.googleapis.com), NOT Vertex AI. Unlike every provider above, Gemini's native API is NOT OpenAI-shaped: requests go to POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent (or :streamGenerateContent?alt=sse for streaming) with the model id in the URL path, and the payload uses contents[]/system_instruction/generationConfig rather than messages[]. So it's the first provider that needs a real IPayloadTranslator (GeminiPayloadTranslator) - see docs/router/unified-api-translation.md §4.3. Auth is the raw key in the x-goog-api-key header (no 'Bearer' prefix); deliberately NOT the ?key= query form, so the secret never lands in a URL. BaseUrl is host-only: the translator builds the full :generateContent path, and ProxyMiddleware forwards to the translator-built URL rather than appending the client's /v1/chat/completions path.

bedrock-anthropic._comment: Anthropic Claude hosted on Amazon Bedrock (docs/router/unified-api-translation.md §4.2). Unlike every provider above, Bedrock is invoked through the AWS SDK (IAmazonBedrockRuntime), not a forwarded HttpRequestMessage - the SDK handles AWS SigV4 request signing and endpoint resolution itself, so there is no ApiKey/ApiKeyEnvVar/AuthHeaderName credential to configure the usual way. BaseUrl/AuthHeaderName below are unused placeholders present only to satisfy ModelRoutingOptions.EnsureValid's provider-wide 'must have a BaseUrl and AuthHeaderName' check. AwsAccessKeyIdEnvVar/AwsSecretAccessKeyEnvVar/AwsSessionTokenEnvVar are an optional explicit credential override; when unset (the default here), the Bedrock Runtime SDK client falls back to its own default AWS credential chain (environment variables, ~/.aws/credentials profiles, instance/container role, etc.), so a from-scratch install works with ambient AWS credentials without editing this file.

bedrock-titan._comment: Amazon Titan Text hosted on Bedrock (docs/router/unified-api-translation.md §4.2). Same AWS-SDK-invocation model as bedrock-anthropic above - see its _comment for why BaseUrl/AuthHeaderName are unused placeholders and how AWS credentials resolve.

bedrock-llama._comment: Meta Llama hosted on Bedrock (docs/router/unified-api-translation.md §4.2). Same AWS-SDK-invocation model as bedrock-anthropic above - see its _comment for why BaseUrl/AuthHeaderName are unused placeholders and how AWS credentials resolve.

Storage._comment: Shared top-level storage location for the SQLite database that the price catalog (and the future usage ledger) both open. Deliberately not under PriceCatalog or CostTracking - two settings for one file could disagree. %LOCALAPPDATA% is expanded at startup; a relative path resolves against the application base directory. See docs/router/agent-cost-tracking.md §4.

PriceCatalog._comment: Model price data ingestion. Only 'litellm' is a recognized source today (naming any other is a hard startup error); PollIntervalHours must be 4-12. Enabling/disabling a source is NOT configured here - it lives in the price catalog database and is managed from Governance > Price Sources, so it can be changed without a restart (D6). A leftover Sources:<name>:Enabled key is a hard startup error rather than an ignored one. Sources entries are needed only to override a source's endpoint via Url. See docs/router/model-price-catalog.md.

SpendTracking._comment: Personal-scale running spend total (not a team/org billing system) - logged as terminal output and appended to a local JSON Lines file. Relative LogPath is resolved from the application base directory.

Sandbox._comment: Off-path execution-grounded verifier for live traffic. See docs/router/sandboxed-executor-architecture.md. Execution tiers (1/2) require Linux + cgroups v2 (+ KVM for Tier 2); on other hosts the capability probe forces Tier-0 static analysis only. Live scores are written to router memory under the LiveMemoryPrefix namespace.

Mcp._comment: The MCP (Model Context Protocol) management endpoint: the same provider/model/budget/price-source management as REST /admin/* and the Governance UI, exposed to MCP clients (Claude Desktop/Code, other agents) over a dedicated loopback TLS port. Gated by the same per-user bearer token that now also guards /admin/* (see docs/router/mcp-endpoint.md) - credentials are write-only on both surfaces.
